newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan welcomes U.S. shuttle diplomacy.
newsitem.headline: Jordan welcomes U.S. shuttle diplomacy.

text.p: Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan said on Saturday the kingdom hoped Washington's renewed shuttle diplomacy would bring progress in stalled Middle East peace talks.

"I think the U.S. effort is welcomed and there is big hope that it will lead to more direct evaluation by Palestinian and Israeli officials," Prince Hassan told reporters ahead of the arrival of U.S. peace envoy Dennis Ross to the region.
He also expressed satisfaction at signs Israel had eased a border crossing closure between the West Bank and Jordan in the wake of the July 30 suicide bombings in Jerusalem which killed 15 people.
"I am very pleased to see normal activity at the bridges and of course the re-opening of border crossings," he said.
In the aftermath of the bombings, Israel suspended a resumption of its talks with the Palestinians and closed border crossings linking the West Bank and Gaza Strip to its Arab neighbours.
Israel also imposed restrictions on Palestinian travel outside self-rule areas, disrupting trade and preventing tens of thousands of Arab workers from reaching their jobs in the Jewish state.
The crown prince also welcomed a possible visit by U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to the Middle East at the end of August, which is tied to progress in resuming peace talks.
He said King Hussein attached much importance to the role of Washington in bringing the two sides back together for peace talks.

Referring to his talks in Alexandria on Thursday with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and senior officials, Prince Hassan said: "There is the same feeling, the same worry about the situation on the ground."
Jordan and Egypt, the only two Arab states which have peace deals with Israel, have led efforts to ease the latest crisis ahead of Ross's visit to the region starting on Saturday.
Jordan is worried a flare-up in tension in Palestinian territories may have a ripple effect on the kingdom's own security.
Amman maintains strong historic ties with the West Bank, which it ruled before its capture by Israel in the Arab-Israeli War in 1967.
